title: The Company's Servant
description: Off the ship at York with a five-year contract and the Factor's eye on you, then up the rivers to Edmonton House, where the Nor'Westers live a stone's throw away and the Beaver Hills Cree decide whose friends they are. Or come up with the North West brigade and be sent to Fort Souris, in the pemmican country where the Pemmican War begins. The history runs underneath both.

beats.title: The Blackfoot take horses from the Beaver Hills camp
beats.rumour: The Beaver Hills Cree are watching their horse herd at night.

happens.text: Word comes in to Edmonton House: Blackfoot raiders have run off the Beaver Hills Cree horse herd, and a young man is dead. The chief's people are asking for you.

beats.title: Grant's Métis plunder Brandon House
beats.rumour: Grant's riders are gathering on the Qu'Appelle, and Brandon House lies on their road.

then.why: for the North West Company and the pemmican

happens.text: Grant's Métis have fallen on Brandon House and carried off its pemmican and furs.
After Seven Oaks the Métis take Fort Douglas, and the colonists are sent down the lake.
Up and down the plains the pemmican war has the camps choosing sides.
The Nor'Westers have broken into Edmonton House's pemmican store in the night and carried off thirty bags.

beats.title: The colony's sheriff seizes the pemmican at Fort Souris
beats.rumour: The colony's sheriff is on the Assiniboine with a warrant and the Brandon House men.

happens.why: the sheriff took the Nor'Westers' pemmican at Fort Souris

happens.text: The colony's sheriff has broken into Fort Souris with the Brandon House men and carried off the pemmican.
Sheriff Spencer has seized the Nor'Westers' pemmican at the Souris under the governor's proclamation.

beats.rumour: The Brûlés are making new sashes and casting ball, and the captains have gone up to the Qu'Appelle.

happens.text: Grant has called the Métis together at the Qu'Appelle. The Brûlés of the Souris are saddling their horses.

questlines.title: The Company's Servant
questlines.summary: From the ship at York to the Company's books at Edmonton House.

quests.title: Report to the Factor
quests.summary: You are the Company's newest servant, and the Factor will want you the hour you land.

on_complete.text: You are on the books of Edmonton House now: six twists of tobacco and four pieces of goods for the road.

objectives.text: Find the Factor and report to him

dialogue.text: {npc} looks you over as he would a new axe. "So you're the Orkney lad. Five years, the contract says. Can you carry, and can you hold your tongue?"

choices.label: "I can do both, sir. Put me to work."
choices.reply: "Good. The ship's boats are at the landing. Every piece to the warehouse, and none of it opened."

choices.label: "I can do both, sir. Put me to work."
choices.reply: "Good. The woodpile is a disgrace. Six loads before you eat."

choices.label: "I signed on for the trade, sir, not the warehouse."
choices.reply: "Every man who ever traded here began in the warehouse. So will you."

choices.label: "I signed on for the trade, sir, not the woodpile."
choices.reply: "Every man who ever traded here began at the woodpile. So will you."

objectives.text: Carry six lots from the ship's boats to the warehouse
Bring six loads of firewood to the woodpile
Report back to the Factor

dialogue.text: {npc} hardly looks up from his ledger. "You'll do. Edmonton House wants hands, and a man who can carry and keep his mouth shut is worth two who can't. You're for the Saskatchewan."

choices.label: "Edmonton House, sir?"
choices.reply: "On the North Saskatchewan, a thousand miles up. The Nor'Westers have Fort Augustus beside it - near enough to hear them sing. The Beaver Hills Cree trade there, and the Blackfoot when they please."

choices.label: "How do I get there?"
choices.reply: "The York boats go up to Cumberland House on the fifth of September; from there you'll find your way. Or walk, if you're a fool. The river is the road."

choices.label: "I'll go, sir."
choices.reply: "Of course you will. The storeman will give you your outfit."

quests.title: Up the rivers
quests.summary: A thousand miles of river between York and Edmonton House.

objectives.text: Go inland to Edmonton House (the York boats leave for Cumberland House on 5 September)

quests.title: Edmonton House
quests.summary: Report to the master of Edmonton House.

objectives.text: Report to the master of Edmonton House

dialogue.text: {npc} reads the York letter twice. "One more mouth, and the winter coming. Well. You'll learn two things here or you'll go home in a box: the Nor'Westers across the way, and the Cree who decide whether we eat. Go and look at both."

choices.label: "I'll go and see them, sir."

questlines.title: The Other House
questlines.summary: The Nor'Westers at Fort Augustus, a stone's throw from your gate.

quests.title: The neighbours
quests.summary: Call at Fort Augustus and see what kind of men the Nor'Westers are.

objectives.text: Call on the master of Fort Augustus

dialogue.text: {npc} meets you at his gate with a pipe in his hand. "So York has sent another clerk to count our canoes. Come in, if you're coming. We don't bite before dinner."

choices.label: Share his pipe and the news from the Bay
Pay your respects and say as little as you can
Tell him to keep his men away from the Company's hunters

do.why: a Company man warned off the Nor'Westers at Fort Augustus

objectives.text: Tell your master how it went

dialogue.text: "Friendly, was he? He is always friendly. Drink his rum and keep your counsel - every word you give him is a word the Company paid for."

objectives.text: Tell your master how it went

dialogue.text: "Said little and heard much? That's the way of it. You'll do here."

objectives.text: Tell your master how it went

dialogue.text: "You told him that? To his face?" {npc} laughs despite himself. "Well, he knows where we stand now. Mind your back on the river."

quests.title: A quiet arrangement
quests.summary: The Nor'Westers' master proposes that neither house carry rum to the Beaver Hills camp this winter, so the Cree trade for goods and not for drink. He asks you to put it to your master.

objectives.text: Put the Nor'Westers' offer to your master

dialogue.text: {npc} hears you out with his arms folded. "No rum to the Beaver Hills camp, theirs or ours. And how do I know they'll keep to it?"

choices.label: Argue for it: a sober camp hunts, and pays its debts

do.why: the houses at Edmonton agree to carry no rum to the Beaver Hills camp

choices.label: Advise against it: the Canadians will break it at the first chance

objectives.text: Take your master's answer to Fort Augustus

dialogue.text: "He agreed? Then you've done a better day's work than either of us." {npc} gives you his hand. "No rum to the Beaver Hills this winter. Let's see who keeps it."

objectives.text: Take your master's answer to Fort Augustus

dialogue.text: {npc} shrugs. "I thought as much. Well, the Cree will drink our rum, then, and pay our debts."

quests.title: Ahead of the Canadians
quests.summary: The Nor'Westers are sending goods out to the Beaver Hills camp. Your master wants the Company's there first.

objectives.text: Carry four pieces of goods to the Beaver Hills Cree before the Nor'Westers' runners

dialogue.text: {npc} looks over the goods. "The Canadians promised us the same. You came first."

on_done.why: the Company beat the Nor'Westers to the Beaver Hills camp

objectives.text: Tell your master the goods are in

dialogue.text: "Good. They'll be sour across the way tonight. Sleep with your knife."

questlines.title: The Company's Friends
questlines.summary: The Beaver Hills Cree, who trade at Edmonton House - and decide whether it eats.

quests.title: Tobacco and talk
quests.summary: Go out to the Beaver Hills Cree camp and make yourself known, as is proper.

on_complete.text: You have sat in council with the Beaver Hills Cree.

objectives.text: Go out to the Beaver Hills Cree camp
Give the chief tobacco, as is proper

dialogue.text: {npc} takes the tobacco, fills a pipe, and passes it to you before he says a word.

objectives.text: Sit with the chief and hear him out

dialogue.text: "The Company's men come and go," {npc} says through the smoke. "Some keep their word. At the last moon the Blackfoot took twenty of our horses, and the Canadians across the river sold them powder. What is the Company's friendship worth?"

choices.label: Say the Company's friendship is not only for trade, and mean it
Promise them the Company's guns
Ask him to teach you the words for it, in Cree

quests.title: The invitation
quests.summary: The buffalo are near, and the Beaver Hills Cree are riding out. Their chief asks whether the Company's man rides with them.

on_complete.text: You rode with the Beaver Hills Cree and ate at their fire. They will remember who stood with them.

objectives.text: Answer the chief's invitation

dialogue.text: "We ride when the scouts come back," {npc} says. "A man who hunts with us eats with us."

choices.label: "I'll ride with you."
"I must ask my master's leave first."

objectives.text: Ask your master's leave to ride with the Cree

dialogue.text: "Go, and bring back meat. A man the Cree hunt with is worth ten the Cree don't."

objectives.text: Ride with the Beaver Hills Cree and bring down a buffalo
Eat with the chief after the hunt

dialogue.text: The meat is shared out, and {npc} gives you the tongue, the best of it. "You ride like a white man, but you ride with us. When the grass is green the Blackfoot will come for horses again. Then we will see who stands with us."

questlines.title: The War
questlines.summary: The Beaver Hills Cree answer for their dead - with you, without you, or not at all.

quests.title: Blood for horses
quests.summary: The Blackfoot have run off the Beaver Hills horses and killed a young man. The chief asks whether the Company's man will ride with them.

objectives.text: Hear what the chief asks of you

dialogue.text: {npc} has cut his hair for the dead boy. "They took our horses and they took my sister's son. When the moon is full my young men ride to the Blackfoot lodges. You ate with us. Will you ride with us?"

choices.label: "I'll ride with you."

do.why: for their dead and their horses

choices.label: "I can't ride with you. But you'll have powder and ball."
"Let me carry a pipe to the Blackfoot first."
"The Company's servants don't go to war."

objectives.text: Lead the Beaver Hills war party south to the Blackfoot camp
Go back to the chief when the fighting is over

dialogue.text: The war party is home. {npc} sits apart from the drums with his pipe, and makes room for you beside him.

choices.label: Sit at the victory dance
Sit with the mourners

objectives.text: Bring the chief four horns of powder (the Edmonton store trades them)

dialogue.text: {npc} weighs the powder horns in his hands. "The Company remembers its friends. So do we."

objectives.text: Tell your master what you have done

dialogue.text: {npc} hears you out. "London does not pay us to take sides in the Indians' wars. But powder is trade, and the Blackfoot would have bought it from the Canadians anyway. Only don't make a habit of it."

objectives.text: Carry a pipe to the Blackfoot camp, a long ride south
Give the Blackfoot chief tobacco

dialogue.text: {npc} smokes your tobacco and waits. He does not smile.

objectives.text: Ask the Blackfoot for peace

dialogue.text: "The Cree killed two of ours at the Red Deer last summer," {npc} says. "Do they remember that? Or does the Company only count the Cree dead?"

choices.label: Ask for a year's peace, and the horses sent back
Demand the horses back, or the Cree will come for them

objectives.text: Bring the Blackfoot answer to the Beaver Hills chief

dialogue.text: "A year." {npc} turns the word over. "Our young men will not like it. But a year is a year of hunting."

objectives.text: Tell the Beaver Hills chief the talks failed

dialogue.text: "Then we have lost nothing but your tobacco." His young men are already painting their horses.

objectives.text: Tell your master you stayed out of it

dialogue.text: "Good. The Company trades with the Blackfoot too, and London hates a war that spoils the returns."

questlines.title: The Pemmican War
questlines.summary: The war between the companies, fought over the pemmican of the plains, comes up the Saskatchewan.

quests.title: News from the Forks
quests.summary: A letter has come up from Red River, and your master wants you.

objectives.text: Hear the news from Red River

dialogue.text: {npc} reads the letter twice before he speaks. "Grant's Métis met Governor Semple at Seven Oaks. Twenty of ours dead, and the governor with them. The Nor'Westers will say they were attacked. Every post on this river is a fort now, theirs and ours."

choices.label: "What would you have me do, sir?"
choices.reply: "Go across and see what they mean to do. Then come and tell me."

objectives.text: Call at Fort Augustus, now that it has come to this

dialogue.text: {npc} has his men under arms at the gate. "You've heard, then. Before God, it was not my doing. What happens here is up to the two of us."

choices.label: Agree that whatever happens at the Forks, Edmonton keeps the peace

do.why: the two houses at Edmonton agree to keep the peace whatever happens at Red River

choices.label: Tell him the North West Company will answer for Seven Oaks

do.why: a Company man promised the Nor'Westers at Edmonton a reckoning for Seven Oaks

objectives.text: Tell your master what was said

dialogue.text: {npc} nods slowly. "Then we know where we stand, which is more than they know at the Forks."

questlines.title: The North Man
questlines.summary: From the brigade's landing to the pemmican country of the Assiniboine.

quests.title: Report to the partner
quests.summary: You are the North West Company's newest clerk, and the partner will want a look at you.

on_complete.text: You are on the books of Fort Souris now: six twists of tobacco and four pieces of goods for the road.

objectives.text: Find the partner and report to him

dialogue.text: {npc} looks up from his letters. "The new clerk. The agents at Montreal write that you can read, write and cast accounts. Out here a man wants a strong back as well. Which have you brought?"

choices.label: "Both, monsieur. Try me."
choices.reply: "We shall. The woodpile first; every bourgeois in the country began at a woodpile, whatever he tells you."

choices.label: "I came up for the trade, monsieur, not to cut wood."
choices.reply: "Then you came up to the wrong country. Six loads, and then we'll talk of trade."

objectives.text: Bring six loads of firewood to the woodpile
Report back to the partner

dialogue.text: {npc} pours two glasses. "You'll do. Fort Souris on the Assiniboine wants a clerk. Pemmican country: every bag that feeds our canoes from Bas de la Rivière to the Athabasca comes off those plains, and the Bay men's Brandon House stands a musket shot from our gate."

choices.label: "What kind of place is Fort Souris, monsieur?"
choices.reply: "Stockades, a store, and more buffalo than you have ever dreamt of. The Brûlés of the Souris - the Métis hunters - camp on the plain above it. Keep them our friends and the post eats; lose them and it starves."

choices.label: "And the Bay men at Brandon House?"
choices.reply: "Honest enough, and slow, and Lord Selkirk's colony at the Forks has given them ideas. They think the plains are theirs because a charter in London says so."

choices.label: "How do I get there?"
choices.reply: "Up to Lake Winnipeg, up the Red to the Forks, and up the Assiniboine until you smell the pemmican. A light canoe, a horse, your own two feet - only get there before the ice."

choices.label: "I'll go, monsieur."
choices.reply: "Of course you will. Take what you need from the store, and don't let the Brûlés beat you at cards."

quests.title: Up the Assiniboine
quests.summary: Lake Winnipeg, the Red, and the Assiniboine between you and Fort Souris.

objectives.text: Go inland to Fort Souris on the Assiniboine

quests.title: Fort Souris
quests.summary: Report to the bourgeois of Fort Souris.

objectives.text: Report to the bourgeois of Fort Souris

dialogue.text: {npc} reads the partner's letter and folds it into his coat. "A clerk. Good. You'll learn two things here: the Bay men at Brandon House, who count every bag we buy, and the Brûlés on the plain, who decide whether there are any bags to buy at all. Go and look at both."

choices.label: "I'll go and see them, monsieur."

questlines.title: The Bay Men
questlines.summary: The Hudson's Bay Company's Brandon House, a musket shot from your gate.

quests.title: The neighbours
quests.summary: Call at Brandon House and see what kind of men the English are.

objectives.text: Call on the master of Brandon House

dialogue.text: {npc} lets you in at the wicket and no further than the yard. "A new Nor'Wester. Have they sent you to count our bags, or to buy our hunters away? Say what you came to say."

choices.label: Offer him a dram and the news from the brigades
Pay your respects and say as little as you can
Tell him the plains traded with the North men before he was born

do.why: a Nor'Wester told the Brandon House master the plains belong to the North men

objectives.text: Tell the bourgeois how it went

dialogue.text: "A dram with the English, was it? Drink his tea, if he gives you any, and remember that every word you leave in that yard goes down to the Forks in his next letter."

objectives.text: Tell the bourgeois how it went

dialogue.text: "Said little and heard much? You'll do here."

objectives.text: Tell the bourgeois how it went

dialogue.text: {npc} laughs until he coughs. "To his face? Well, he knows where we stand. Keep your gun by your bed."

quests.title: One bag, one price
quests.summary: The master of Brandon House proposes that neither house outbid the other for the Métis pemmican this winter. He asks you to put it to your bourgeois.

objectives.text: Put the Bay men's offer to your bourgeois

dialogue.text: {npc} hears you out with his pipe going hard. "One price for a bag of pemmican, theirs and ours. And the day the brigades are hungry, who keeps to it?"

choices.label: Argue for it: a bidding war only fattens the Brûlés and empties both stores

do.why: the houses on the Souris agree on one price for pemmican

choices.label: Advise against it: the English will break it the first lean month

objectives.text: Take your bourgeois's answer to Brandon House

dialogue.text: "He agreed?" {npc} shakes your hand over the gate. "Then the Brûlés will have to get rich some other way. Let's see which of us keeps it."

objectives.text: Take your bourgeois's answer to Brandon House

dialogue.text: {npc} only nods. "I thought as much. Well, the Brûlés will do well out of the two of us this winter."

quests.title: Ahead of the English
quests.summary: Brandon House is sending goods out to the Métis camp. Your bourgeois wants the North men's there first.

objectives.text: Carry four pieces of goods to the Métis camp before the Bay men's cart

dialogue.text: {npc} turns the goods over. "The English promised us the same. You came first, and the Brûlés remember who comes first."

on_done.why: the Nor'Westers beat Brandon House to the Métis camp

objectives.text: Tell the bourgeois the goods are in

dialogue.text: "Good. They'll be sour at Brandon House tonight. Sleep with your knife."

questlines.title: The New Nation
questlines.summary: The Métis hunters of the Souris - the Bois-Brûlés - who run the buffalo and make the pemmican.

quests.title: Tobacco on the plain
quests.summary: Ride out to the Métis camp on the Souris plain and make yourself known.

on_complete.text: You have smoked with the Métis of the Souris.

objectives.text: Ride out to the Métis camp on the Souris plain
Give the hunt captain tobacco

dialogue.text: {npc} takes the tobacco with a grin. "A clerk who knows his manners. Sit down, bourgeois, the kettle's on."

objectives.text: Sit with the captain and hear him out

dialogue.text: "My father was a trader out of Boston; my mother's people were here before any of you," {npc} says. "Now the Bay men's lord has a colony at the Forks and a paper that says this plain is his. We run the buffalo here. We make the pemmican. Whose plain is it, bourgeois?"

choices.label: Say the plain belongs to those who hunt it, and the North men will stand by them
Promise them the North West Company's guns
Ask him to teach you how the Brûlés run the buffalo

quests.title: The hunt
quests.summary: The scouts have found the herds, and the Métis of the Souris are going out on the hunt, carts, captains and all. The captain asks whether the clerk rides with them.

on_complete.text: You ran the buffalo with the Métis of the Souris. They will remember who stood with them.

objectives.text: Answer the captain

dialogue.text: "The laws of the hunt," {npc} says, counting on his fingers. "Nobody runs before the signal. Nobody leaves the camp alone. The captain's word is the law until the meat is in. Still want to come?"

choices.label: "I'll keep the laws. I'm coming."
"I must ask the bourgeois first."

objectives.text: Ask the bourgeois's leave to go on the hunt

dialogue.text: "Go! And count the bags they make. Every one of them is a bag the Bay men don't get."

objectives.text: Ride with the Métis of the Souris and bring down a buffalo
Eat with the captain after the hunt

dialogue.text: The women are already cutting the meat into strips for the drying racks. {npc} hands you a marrow bone. "You ride like a clerk, but you ride. Remember who you ate with, bourgeois. A day is coming when the Bay men's governor tells us we cannot sell our own pemmican, and then we'll see who stands with us."

questlines.title: The Pemmican War
questlines.summary: The colony's governor forbids the pemmican to leave the plains, and the North men will not starve to oblige him.

quests.title: The proclamation
quests.summary: The governor at the Forks has forbidden any pemmican to leave Assiniboia, and Fort Souris has a full store.

objectives.text: Hear what the bourgeois means to do about the proclamation

dialogue.text: {npc} has the governor's paper pinned to his table with a knife. "Macdonell forbids any pemmican to leave his colony's lands - and he says his colony's lands run from the Forks to God knows where. Our store is full, and the brigades eat it or the brigades stop. He'll send his sheriff for it."

choices.label: "Then let's not keep it all in the store. The Brûlés can hide it on the plain."
"Let him come. We'll hold the gate."

do.why: the Nor'Westers at Fort Souris swear to hold their pemmican

choices.label: "It's the law of the country now, monsieur. Better to sell to them than fight them."

do.why: a Nor'Wester at Fort Souris spoke for obeying the proclamation

objectives.text: Carry the first bags out to the Métis camp, to be hidden on the plain

dialogue.text: {npc} grins at the bags. "Hide pemmican from the English on our own plain? My grandmother could do it."

objectives.text: Tell the bourgeois you'll stand by him

dialogue.text: "Whatever comes, we're Nor'Westers first," {npc} says, and pours. "Drink to the partners."

quests.title: The sheriff
quests.summary: The colony's sheriff has come to Fort Souris with the Brandon House men and carried off the pemmican.

objectives.text: Hear what happened at the gate

dialogue.text: The gate hangs open on one hinge. {npc} is white with anger. "Spencer, the colony's sheriff, with the Brandon House men and their axes. A warrant, he said. They carried every bag they could find across to Brandon House, and the Bay men stood and watched."

choices.label: "I'll go to Brandon House and ask for it back."
"The Brûlés will want to hear of this."
"Write to the partners, monsieur. Let the law answer the law."

objectives.text: Ask the master of Brandon House for the pemmican back

dialogue.text: {npc} won't meet your eye. "It's under the governor's seal now. I can't touch it - and I didn't ask for it, whatever you think."

choices.label: Ask him quietly, as a neighbour, for enough to feed your own men

do.why: the Brandon House master quietly sent back some of the seized pemmican

choices.label: Tell him the North men will take it back, seal or no seal

do.why: a Nor'Wester promised to take back the seized pemmican by force

objectives.text: Carry the news to the Métis camp

dialogue.text: {npc} listens without a word, then spits. "Our pemmican. Our plain. And a sheriff with a paper." Behind him the young men have stopped what they were doing.

quests.title: The Brûlés ride
quests.summary: Grant has called the Métis together. They mean to bring the pemmican through to the canoes, and Brandon House is on the road.

objectives.text: Hear what the captain asks of you

dialogue.text: {npc} has a new sash and a new musket. "Grant calls the Brûlés together. We take the pemmican down the Assiniboine to the canoes, and if the Bay men stand in the road, we go through them. Brandon House first. You ate with us. Will you ride with us?"

choices.label: "I'll ride with you."

do.why: for the pemmican and the North West Company

choices.label: "The post needs me here."

do.why: for the pemmican and the North West Company

choices.label: Say nothing - and go and warn Brandon House

objectives.text: Ride with the Métis of the Souris to Brandon House
Find the captain when it is over

dialogue.text: The carts are loaded and the horses watered. {npc} sits on a pemmican bag with his musket across his knees.

choices.label: Help load Brandon House's pemmican onto the carts
Help with the wounded

objectives.text: Tell the bourgeois you stayed

dialogue.text: "Wise," {npc} says, watching the dust of the carts on the road east. "A clerk who rides with Grant may find himself in a Montreal court one day. Let the Brûlés do what the Brûlés do."

objectives.text: Warn the master of Brandon House that the Brûlés are coming

dialogue.text: {npc} goes grey. "How many? When?" He is already shouting for his men to bar the gate. "I won't forget this. I don't know if your own people will."

on_done.why: for the pemmican and the North West Company

quests.title: Seven Oaks
quests.summary: Word has come up the Assiniboine from the Forks.

objectives.text: Hear the news from the Forks

dialogue.text: {npc} has the letter open and does not look up. "Grant's men met Governor Semple at Seven Oaks. Twenty of theirs dead, and the governor with them; one of ours. The partners say the colonists fired first. Selkirk will say otherwise, and Selkirk has the ear of London."

choices.label: "They fired first. The Brûlés defended themselves."
"Twenty men dead, monsieur. Whoever fired first, it was murder."

objectives.text: Go across to Brandon House, now that it has come to this

dialogue.text: {npc} meets you at the gate with a musket. "Seven Oaks. You've heard. Before God, if one of you lifts a hand to this house again, we'll answer it."

choices.label: Promise that whatever happens at the Forks, the Souris keeps the peace

do.why: the two houses on the Souris agree to keep the peace whatever happens at the Forks

choices.label: Tell him the Bay men brought this on themselves with their proclamation

do.why: a Nor'Wester at Brandon House blamed Seven Oaks on the proclamation

objectives.text: Tell the bourgeois what was said

dialogue.text: {npc} grunts. "Selkirk is coming up the lakes with soldiers, they say - hired Swiss, out of the war. Whatever we've done, we'd best be able to account for it."

questlines.title: The Lawless Years
questlines.summary: Selkirk's soldiers, the Grand Rapids, and the union of the two companies.

quests.title: Selkirk's soldiers
quests.summary: Lord Selkirk has taken Fort William, and Fort Augustus across the way is short of everything.

objectives.text: Hear the news from the Lakes

dialogue.text: {npc} has a letter from Norway House. "Lord Selkirk came up the lakes with his Swiss and took Fort William. McGillivray and the partners are arrested and sent down to Canada. The Nor'Westers' heart is cut out - and Fort Augustus will have a hungry winter of it, with no goods coming up."

choices.label: "Then this is the winter to take the Beaver Hills trade from them."
"They'll be short of food. Lend them pemmican, as neighbours."
"Let London and Montreal settle it, sir."

objectives.text: Carry the Company's goods out to the Beaver Hills camp, on easy credit

dialogue.text: {npc} looks at the goods, then at you. "The Canadians have nothing this year, and you come with gifts. The Company is a good friend when it is the only friend."

on_done.why: the Company took the Beaver Hills trade while Fort Augustus went short

objectives.text: Carry four bags of pemmican across to Fort Augustus

dialogue.text: {npc} looks at the bags a long while. "I won't forget this. Whatever they do to each other in London, I won't forget it."

on_done.why: the Company lent pemmican to the hungry Nor'Westers at Fort Augustus

quests.title: The Grand Rapids
quests.summary: Governor Williams means to stop the Nor'Westers' partners on their way down the Saskatchewan, and he wants men.

objectives.text: Hear what the Governor asks

dialogue.text: {npc} reads you the Governor's letter. "Williams means to wait for the Nor'Westers' partners at the Grand Rapids, where the river comes down into the lake, with the Swiss and a field gun, and take them as they come down with their furs. Every post is to send men. They muster at Cumberland House."

choices.label: "I'll go down to Cumberland House."
"Someone has to hold Edmonton, sir."

objectives.text: Go down the Saskatchewan to the muster at Cumberland House
Report to the master of Cumberland House

dialogue.text: {npc} jerks his head at the storehouse. "You're late for the fight: Williams took them at the Rapids, Shaw and McDonald and the rest, with their canoes. Frobisher got clear and ran into the bush. The prisoners are in there. Somebody has to watch them tonight."

choices.label: Stand the night watch over the prisoners
Leave the storehouse door unbarred, and look the other way

quests.title: One company
quests.summary: London and Montreal have made one company of the two. Edmonton and Fort Augustus are to be one house.

then.text: Fort Augustus came into Edmonton as friends: you had been a neighbour to them when it counted.
Fort Augustus came into Edmonton as a beaten house, and its men did not forget who had beaten it.
The Beaver Hills Cree remember the year you stood with them against the Blackfoot.
The Beaver Hills Cree still call you a friend, one company or two.
You stood watch over the North West partners at Cumberland House. Some of them are your masters now.

on_complete.text: So ends the story of the Company's servant. The country goes on.

objectives.text: Hear the news of the union

dialogue.text: {npc} reads the letter out to the whole post. "The Company and the North West Company are one, under the Company's charter. Mr. Simpson governs the Northern Department. Fort Augustus comes into Edmonton. Half the men on the river, theirs and ours, will be let go." He folds the letter. "Go across and tell them. They'll have heard, but go."

choices.label: "I'll go across."

objectives.text: Go across to Fort Augustus, now that it is one company

dialogue.text: {npc} is packing his books into a trunk. "So. Twenty years of it, and the Bay has us after all."

choices.label: Shake his hand: you'll sit at one mess now
Tell him it's the Bay's house now, and he can carry his own trunk
Help him carry his books across to Edmonton

objectives.text: Go out to the Beaver Hills camp with the news

dialogue.text: {npc} hears it with no surprise. "One company. Then there is nobody to take our furs to when you give too little. You will see the prices fall, and you will tell us it is London."

choices.label: Promise him you'll deal fairly while you're at Edmonton, whatever London says
Tell him the truth: the prices will be London's now

questlines.title: The Reckoning
questlines.summary: Fort William taken, warrants and ambushes, and the end of the North West Company.

quests.title: Fort William
quests.summary: Lord Selkirk has taken Fort William and arrested the partners.

objectives.text: Hear the news from Fort William

dialogue.text: {npc} has not slept. "Selkirk came up the lakes with his Swiss and took Fort William. McGillivray arrested, the partners sent down to Canada in irons, the goods for the whole interior under a lord's seal. They're drinking to it at Brandon House."

choices.label: "Then we hold what we have, and wait for Montreal."

do.why: the Nor'Westers at Fort Souris mean to hold what they have

choices.label: "Make our peace with Brandon House while we still can."

objectives.text: Go across to Brandon House to talk of peace

dialogue.text: {npc} hears you out at the gate. "Peace? With Selkirk's soldiers on the lakes, you come asking for peace." He looks at you a while. "Well. Neither of us has ever shot the other. Let's keep it so."

on_done.why: the houses on the Souris made their own peace after Fort William fell

quests.title: The warrant
quests.summary: A constable from the colony is at Brandon House with warrants from Selkirk's magistrates, and your name is on one.

objectives.text: Hear what the bourgeois has to tell you

dialogue.text: {npc} closes the door before he speaks. "There's a constable at Brandon House from the Forks, with warrants signed by Selkirk's own magistrates - for every man who rode with Grant, or stood up for him. Your name is on one."

choices.label: "The Brûlés will hide me."
"I'll go and answer it. I've nothing to be ashamed of."
"Let him come and take me."

do.why: a Nor'Wester at Fort Souris defied the colony's warrant

objectives.text: Ride out to the Métis camp and lie low
Ask the captain to hide you

dialogue.text: {npc} laughs. "A constable from the Forks, looking for one man on this plain? Let him look. You'll sleep in my lodge, and if he comes, you're my cousin from Pembina."

objectives.text: Go to Brandon House and answer the warrant

dialogue.text: The constable reads out the warrant. {npc} stands by with his arms folded. "You'll give your word not to run, and the case goes down to Canada with the rest." He lowers his voice. "Half of them are thrown out there. Montreal juries don't love the Earl."

quests.title: The Grand Rapids
quests.summary: The Bay men have ambushed the partners coming down the Saskatchewan.

objectives.text: Hear the news from the Saskatchewan

dialogue.text: {npc}'s voice is flat. "Governor Williams waited for our partners at the Grand Rapids with the Swiss and a field gun, and took them as they came down with the furs. Frobisher got away into the bush. They found him dead of cold and hunger."

choices.label: "Then we pay them back, here, at Brandon House."

do.why: the Nor'Westers on the Souris swear to answer the Grand Rapids

choices.label: "This war is killing both companies, monsieur."

quests.title: The coalition
quests.summary: It is done: the North West Company goes into the Hudson's Bay Company.

then.text: Brandon House took you in as one of its own. You had been a neighbour to it when it counted.
Brandon House took you on its books and never let you forget the summer the Brûlés came.
You went out to the Métis of the Souris as a freeman, and ran the buffalo with them for the Bay as you had for the North men.
You went down to Montreal with your wages, one of the hundreds the union let go.
Grant's name and yours are written together in the Pemmican War, for good or ill.
The Métis of the Souris still call you a friend.

on_complete.text: So ends the story of the North man. The country goes on.

objectives.text: Hear the news from Montreal

dialogue.text: {npc} reads the letter, and reads it again. "It is done. The North West Company goes into the Hudson's Bay Company. The partners are to be chief factors and chief traders. The clerks and the men are to be counted, and many let go. Fort Souris closes; Brandon House keeps the trade." He puts the letter down. "What will you do?"

choices.label: "Sign the Bay's articles, and go across to Brandon House."
"Go out to the Métis and live as a freeman."
"Take my wages and go down to Montreal."

objectives.text: Go across to Brandon House, a Bay man now

dialogue.text: {npc} looks at you over the books, a long look.

choices.label: Take the hand he offers
Meet his eye, and say nothing about the summer of 1816
Ask him where he wants you

objectives.text: Ride out to the Métis camp with your wages and your gun
Tell the captain you've come to stay

dialogue.text: {npc} looks at your bundle and your gun and grins. "A freeman. Well, there are worse things to be. The Bay will want our pemmican as much as the North men did. More, maybe."
